recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-12591 unless a separate work-group decision chooses to clean stale copied Restrictions worksheet rows that do not drive the current Age datatype definition.
issue_request: FHIR-12591 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core datatypes change request raised against DSTU2. It reported that the Age invariant's FHIRPath expression checked for a decimal point even though Age.value must be positive, and the accepted resolution was to change the value term to value > 0.
initial_application: The Jira comments cite svn revision 11174. In Git history, commit 3ad0995feb09c65e27f0c9cd6512acb34e24b248 (#12591 - fix age invariant) changed source/datatypes/age.xml from value.toString().contains('.').not() to value > 0 in the Age invariant expression.
additional_context: Age is active in source/fhir.ini and source/datatypes/age.xml is the authoritative current Age datatype spreadsheet. Later FHIR-15648 refined the same invariant to use code.exists() and value.hasValue().not() while preserving the FHIR-12591 positive-value clause. A stale Age-looking row remains in source/datatypes/distance.xml's Restrictions worksheet, but the active Age source and released profile history files contain the corrected expression, so that row was not treated as a current FHIR-12591 source fix.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The current Age invariant row already reads (code.exists() or value.empty()) and (system.empty() or system = %ucum) and (value.empty() or value.hasValue().not() or value > 0), which preserves the accepted FHIR-12591 semantics after later invariant refinements.

related_jiras.note: Later Published/Persuasive correction to the same Age invariant changed code to code.exists() and preserved the FHIR-12591 positive-value clause; it is already represented on the combined branch by commit 1fa17c9bc81f8d7a7b77bcadbf91437b2cb7fc40.
